explanation: The statement is about the library's own definition `cindex` (the argument-principle integral `(2πi)⁻¹ ∮_{C(z₀,r)} f'/f`), comparing it with the `FormalMultilinearSeries.order` of a power series of `f` at `z₀`. I searched Mathlib extensively: `cindex` appears nowhere; there is no argument principle / winding number / zero-counting formula for circle integrals of `deriv f / f` (greps for `cindex`, `windingNumber`, `∮ ... deriv ... f`, `deriv f z / f z`, `logDeriv` — which only occurs in `LocallyUniformLimit`); the circle-integral files (`Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/CircleIntegral.lean`, `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/CauchyIntegral.lean`, `RemovableSingularity.lean`, `Liouville.lean`, `JensenFormula.lean`, `ValueDistribution/*`) contain no theorem equating such an integral with an order. Mathlib's `FormalMultilinearSeries.order` lemmas (`order_eq_zero_iff`, `eq_pow_order_mul_iterate_dslope`, `locally_zero_iff`, etc.) supply ingredients only, not this result; deriving it would need the substantial argument-principle computation carried out in this file (`cindex_eq_order_aux`, `exists_cindex_eq_order'`). Hence no duplicate and no single-declaration derivation.
